label: Link
title: Link
summary: Use a Link to send people to related content, such as terms, help, or a recovery step, on its own line or inside a sentence.
corePrinciple: Links take people somewhere. Keep the screen’s main action a Button.

anatomy.title: An underlined label
anatomy.description: Link is a single run of text in the same colour as the copy around it. The Text Sizes mode sets its size, and it is always underlined.
blocks: Says where the link goes; its size follows the Text Sizes mode.
Always on; it is the cue that the words can be pressed.
With Fill, the link spans its parent, so the whole row responds to a press.

configuration.title: Choose the width and alignment
configuration.description: Fill stretches the link across its parent, the only width where Center has room to work. Hug keeps it to its words. Inside a sentence, the link flows with the copy.
blocks: The default. The label starts at the left and the whole row is pressable.
Centres the label, for example under a full-width button.
Only the words are pressable, for a link in a row beside other content.
Inside a TextSegment the link wraps with the copy and takes its colour and size.

states.title: Enabled and disabled
states.description: Disable a link only while it briefly can’t be used, such as Resend code during a countdown. Links have no pressed, hover, or visited style.

sizing.title: The parent sets the width; the type sets the height
sizing.description: A Fill link is as wide as its parent and a Hug link as wide as its words. Its height is one line of type: 16, 17, or 24 px for Small, Medium, and Large. Long labels wrap onto more lines.

content.title: Say where it goes
content.description: Write a short label in sentence case that names the destination or task, such as “Forgot PIN?” or “View all transactions”. In a sentence, link only the words that name the destination and keep the punctuation outside. Avoid vague labels such as “Click here”.

inContext.title: Terms and help on a confirmation card
inContext.description: The screen opens the Terms, Privacy Policy, or help when a link is pressed; Link only reports the press. The main action stays a Button.

doDont.title: Keep links clear and secondary
doDont.description: Each pair shows a link people can find and act on versus one that misleads them.
blocks: Only “Terms” and “Privacy Policy” are underlined, so people know what opens.
A fully underlined sentence hides what will open.
The Fill link centres its label under the button.
A Hug link has no room to centre, so it stays at the left.
Keep the main action a Button
Continue stands out, and the link offers a way out.
Make the main action a link
A 17 px underlined line is easy to miss and hard to tap.

sources.title: Use the public Link contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Declared and installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 from the team’s private package repository. Figma has three variants (Left and Fill, Left and Hug, Center and Fill) and no disabled variant; the package adds disabled. The screen handles navigation in onPress; Link has no web address or target. On the web, Enter and Space activate a focused link, and a disabled link is announced as disabled and skipped by Tab.
